(Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, you can start studying for the test at any time. The official study guide, Discover Canada: The Rights and Responsibilities of Citizenship, is available in multiple formats, including:

- reading the study guide online
- downloading the PDF or eBook for offline viewing
- listening to the audio version
- ordering a paper copy (Source: Citizenship test: Study for the test, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/canadian-citizenship/test/study.html).

The following organizations are designated for educational credential assessment for immigration purposes:

1. Comparative Education Service – University of Toronto School of Continuing Studies (designated on April 17, 2013)
2. International Credential Assessment Service of Canada (designated on April 17, 2013)
3. World Education Services (designated on April 17, 2013)
4. International Qualifications Assessment Service (IQAS) (designated on August 6, 2015)
5. International Credential Evaluation Service – British Columbia Institute of Technology (designated on August 6, 2015)

(Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, you are eligible for a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) if you complete a Bachelor of Christian Ministry at Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary and College and meet all other PGWP criteria. (Source: Canadian Baptist Theological Seminary and College, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/study-permit/prepare/designated-learning-institutions-list/canadian-southern-baptist-seminary-college.html)

No, you cannot maintain your temporary resident status while your temporary resident permit (TRP) application is being processed. This applies to both initial TRP applications and any other TRP applications. (Source: Visitor record: After you apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/extend-stay/after-apply.html)

Yes, you need an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) for immigration purposes if you completed your education outside Canada. An ECA is used to verify that your foreign degree, diploma, or certificate is valid and equal to a Canadian one. It helps you earn points for education you got outside Canada, or for your spouse or common-law partner’s education, if they are coming with you to Canada. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, it counts as a participation if you arrive in Canada and get your work permit. If you are approved but do not come to Canada to get a work permit, that does not count as a participation. (Source: International Experience Canada: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/eligibility.html)

Yes, you can apply for a super visa while you wait for a decision or withdraw your sponsorship application at any time and apply for a super visa. (Source: Super visa for parents and grandparents: Who can apply, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/parent-grandparent-super-visa/eligibility.html)

No, if you hire a worker through the Provincial Nominee Program (PNP), they must settle in the province or territory that nominated them. (Source: Hire a provincial nominee, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-permanent-foreign/provincial-nominee.html)

To enter more than one educational credential in your Express Entry profile, follow these steps:

1. Go to the Study and languages form in your profile.
2. Fill in all the fields in the Education history section with your first credential.
3. Use the credential for your highest degree, diploma or certificate.
4. Click Save and add. The fields you just filled out will go blank.
5. Your credential will appear in the Education history table below the Save and add button.
6. Repeat steps 1 to 3 for all your remaining educational credentials.

You can’t submit more than 1 educational credential in the same field. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, as an international student, you can work for a private business on campus. An "on campus" employer can be a private business, as long as it provides on-campus services to the school. (Source: Work on campus as an international student, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/study-canada/work/work-on-campus.html)

Yes, you can apply for the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you are working in Canada on an LMIA-exempt work permit and have been employed full-time for the same employer for 1 year. You must also meet the following conditions:

- Your work permit is valid both when you apply and when the permanent resident visa is issued (or you’re allowed to work in Canada without a permit when your permanent resident visa is issued).
- Your current employer has made a valid job offer based on you being accepted as a skilled worker.
- You are currently working for the employer specified on your work permit.
- You have been working for that employer for at least 1 year, continuous full-time or part-time equivalent.

(Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, you must provide an electronic signature when uploading additional documents for your International Experience Canada work permit application. If you don’t, your application won’t be processed. (Source: International Experience Canada: Submit your work permit application, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/iec/apply-work-permit.html)

Yes, you can apply for the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you're currently working in Canada on a work permit based on a positive LMIA in a TEER category 0, 1, 2 or 3 occupation, and your employer has made a valid job offer. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, if your post-secondary credential is not equal to a Canadian credential, you can get your secondary credential assessed to get points for completing secondary school. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, if your work permit renewal application is still being processed, you may be allowed to re-enter Canada as a visitor. However, you cannot work until your work permit renewal has been approved. (Source: Extend or change the conditions on your work permit: Traveling outside Canada and re-entering, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/extend/travel-outside-canada.html)

To find the points you can earn in the Comprehensive Ranking System based on your educational credential assessment report, you can use the table provided on the IRCC website. The table shows the possible results for an educational credential assessment report and their corresponding points. You can select the points system you would like to see, enter your result in the “Filter items” field, and choose the assessment result that matches your report. The level of education for your Express Entry profile and points will show beside the result. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

No, you do not need a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA) to hire a seasonal overnight camp counsellor from June to September under the International Mobility Program. The offer of employment must be for seasonal employment (usually from June to September), the occupation camp counsellor or a similar job title (NOC 5254), and a residential camp (overnight camp that lasts more than 1 weekend). (Source: Hiring an overnight camp counsellor through the International Mobility Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/work-canada/hire-temporary-foreign/international-mobility-program/how-to-hire/residential-camp-counsellor.html)

Yes, you can apply for a work permit without an AOR if you meet both of the following criteria:
- Your work or study permit, or temporary resident status will expire in 2 weeks or less, and
- You’ve applied for permanent residence under the Spouse or Common-Law Partner in Canada class (SCLPC) or the Family Class as a spouse, common-law or conjugal partner. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

No, you must pay the Right of Permanent Residence fee when you submit your application. Yes, you can include part-time work experience towards the Federal Skilled Worker Program if you worked more than 15 hours a week but less than 30 hours a week, as long as it adds up to 1,560 hours. You can work more than one part-time job to get the hours you need to apply. (Source: Express Entry: Federal Skilled Worker Program, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/who-can-apply/federal-skilled-workers.html)

Yes, you can apply for an open work permit if you are being sponsored for permanent residence and living in Canada with your sponsor. You must also be in a genuine relationship with your sponsor, included in an application for permanent residence, and have an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter confirming that your permanent residence application is being processed. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Yes, to be eligible for an open work permit as a dependent child, you must meet both of these requirements:
- The principal applicant you’re accompanying must be
- in a genuine relationship with their sponsor
- included in an application for permanent residence, and have an AOR letter confirming that their permanent residence application is being processed
- It’s the AOR their sponsor receives from IRCC.
- living in Canada with their sponsor
- You must be living with your family member (the principal applicant) and their sponsor. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Yes, as a specialist in clinical and laboratory medicine (NOC code 31100), specialist in surgery (NOC code 31101), or general practitioner or family physician (NOC code 31102), you must get an ECA report from the Medical Council of Canada for your primary medical diploma. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, you can extend your open work permit for 2 more years under this public policy if you meet all of the following criteria:

- You received your AOR for your permanent residence application.
- Your permanent residence application is still being processed.
- This means that no decision has been made on your application.

(Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

No, if you are an architect (NOC 21200) but do not need a license to work as a project manager at a construction firm, one of the other designated organizations can assess your credentials. A certified translator is a member in good standing of a professional translation association in Canada or abroad. Their certification must be confirmed by a seal or stamp that shows the translator’s membership number. Yes, your Express Entry profile can become ineligible if your work experience is no longer within the 3 years before you apply. You must also be in a genuine relationship with your sponsor, included in an application for permanent residence, and have an acknowledgement of receipt (AOR) letter confirming that your permanent residence application is being processed. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Όχι, δεν μπορείτε να υποβάλετε αίτηση για eTA στις 13 Οκτωβρίου 2026 από τις 12.00 π.μ. έως τις 5.30 π.μ. (Ανατολική Ώρα), επειδή η κυβέρνηση του Καναδά θα πραγματοποιεί ενημερώσεις στο ηλεκτρονικό της σύστημα κατά τη διάρκεια αυτής της χρονικής περιόδου. (Source: Αίτηση Ηλεκτρονικής Ταξιδιωτικής Άδειας (eTA), https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/visit-canada/eta/apply-el.html)

Yes, the principal applicant (your child's sponsor) must have an AOR letter confirming that their permanent residence application is being processed. The AOR letter is for the principal applicant's permanent resident application, which is the one they receive from IRCC. (Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

Yes, as a family physician (NOC 31102) applying for immigration, you need to get an Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) report from the Medical Council of Canada for your primary medical diploma. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

Yes, you can extend your open work permit for 2 more years under this public policy if you meet all the following criteria:

- You received your AOR for your permanent residence application.
- Your permanent residence application is still being processed.
- This means that no decision has been made on your application.

(Source: Sponsor your spouse, partner or child: Optional: Open work permit in Canada, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/family-sponsorship/spouse-partner-children/spouse-common-law-partner-canada-open-work-permit.html)

No, you do not need the Canadian Architectural Certification Board (CACB) to assess your credentials if you are an architect (NOC 21200) but you do not need a license to work as a project manager at a construction firm. (Source: Educational credential assessment, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/documents/education-assessment.html)

A certified translator is a member in good standing of a professional translation association in Canada or abroad. Their certification must be confirmed by a seal or stamp that shows the translator’s membership number. (Source: Apply for permanent residence through Express Entry, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/apply-permanent-residence.html)

Yes, your Express Entry profile can become ineligible if your work experience is no longer within the 3 years before you apply. This is one of the common reasons why your profile may become ineligible. (Source: Express Entry: Create your profile and enter the pool, https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/immigrate-canada/express-entry/create-profile.html)

The TEER categories required for skilled work experience in the Federal Skilled Worker Program are 0, 1, 2, or 3 of the National Occupational Classification (NOC).
